title: This Fish Shoots Insects Out of the Air From 6 Feet Away

scenes.text: This fish shoots insects out of the air with water.
The archerfish hits a bug on a branch six and a half feet away.
Its mouth works like a gun barrel. It squeezes so the back of the jet catches up with the front.
The water bunches into a heavy blob right as it lands. Six times the power of the fish's own muscles.
Grasshoppers clinging with ten times their weight get knocked into the river.
All from under the surface, through the ripples. Every shot is a trick shot.

description:
The archerfish knocks insects off branches with a jet of water from up to 2 metres, about 6.5 feet, away.
Researchers at the University of Bayreuth found the fish shapes the jet with its mouth so the water piles up into a dense blob just before impact, delivering about six times the power its muscles could produce on their own, enough to dislodge prey that grips with ten times its own weight.
Which animal has the most unfair hunting weapon?
thumbnail_text: A FISH WITH A WATER GUN
first_comment: The front of the jet leaves at about 2 metres a second, and the fish keeps pushing so the back catches up at the last moment. Have you ever seen an archerfish in an aquarium?
